newsitem.title: USA: Clinton administration backs Calif. rail project.
newsitem.headline: Clinton administration backs Calif. rail project.

text.p: The Clinton administration on Tuesday signed a $750 million full funding grant agreement that will enable a San Francisco suburban rail system to be extended to the city's airport, officials said.

Two California legislators, Sen. Barbara Boxer and Rep. Nancy Pelosi, announced that Transportation Secretary Rodney Slater had signed an agreement with Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) to extend the network to San Francisco International Airport.
Although federal funding requires congressional approval, Boxer said the full funding grant agreement was "a commitment by the administration to stand 100 percent behind this project."

"The BART extension will improve the quality of life in the (San Francisco) Bay area by creating 10,000 jobs, relieving traffic congestion, making the environment cleaner and providing easier access to the airport for Bay area travelers," Boxer said in a statement.

Steve Morin, a legislative aide to Pelosi, said the agreement meant the Clinton administration was guaranteeing it would put in its budget over the next eight years $750 million for the BART project. Morin said the agreement would allow BART to sign contracts and borrow money for the project.
The remainder of the funds needed for the $1.2 billion project to build the 8.7-mile (15 km) extension will come from local, regional and state sources.
BART Board President Margaret Pryor hailed the agreement, saying: "This is a proud day, a great day for BART."

BART spokesman Mike Healy said the announcement was "a major step" and meant the agency could finally begin construction of the extension project, which has been studied for more than 20 years but has often been delayed by lawsuits and funding battles.
